# Purpose

This document executes and explains the R implementation of the active Project
02 scientific workflow. It preserves the Python analysis as the source of the
existing published artifacts and writes all R-generated files under
`10_R-workflow/outputs`.

# Data construction

The default run reads the established analytic dataset. Setting
`params$rebuild_data` to `TRUE` reconstructs all derived analysis columns from
the independently extracted WHO profile, WHO screening, and World Bank files.

```{r data}
cascade <- load_or_build_dataset(params$rebuild_data)
data.frame(rows = nrow(cascade), countries = length(unique(cascade$iso3)),
           screening_available = sum(!is.na(cascade$screened_last5y_2019)),
           capacity_available = sum(!is.na(cascade$capacity_mean)))
```

# Prespecified analysis gate

The interaction analysis may proceed only with at least 80 complete countries,
at least a 10-percentage-point screening interquartile range, and at least 10
countries in each extreme capacity tertile.

```{r model}
fits <- fit_project02_models(cascade)
as.data.frame(fits$decision)
```

# Negative-binomial interaction model

The outcome is the 2019 cervical-cancer death count. The model uses the female
population as a log offset and includes screening, downstream capacity, their
interaction, incidence, GDP, registry availability, and WHO-region indicators.

```{r coefficients}
fits$coefficients
```

```{r marginal-effects}
fits$marginal_effects
```

# Outputs and formal Python parity

```{r outputs}
write_project02_outputs(cascade, fits, params$run_uncertainty)
if (params$make_figures) make_project02_figures(cascade, fits)
parity <- verify_project02_parity(cascade, fits)
as.data.frame(parity)
```

# Interpretation safeguards

The negative-binomial interaction is ecological and cross-sectional. The
screening estimates, mortality counts, incidence estimates, and reported
capacity indicators do not represent a linked individual-level cascade. The R
workflow therefore reproduces the model without strengthening its causal
interpretation.
